evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0 h = 4.32 mg/L, down from 10.24 mg/L at 50.0 h (~3 mg/L/h decline)
Receiving P(48 h) = 2.88 g/L, comparable to source P(48 h) ≈ 3.0 g/L — product on track
Source batches maintain DO2 ≈ 10.8–11.5 mg/L at 50–52 h; receiving deviates sharply below
Minimum DO2 constraint = 2.0 mg/L; projected breach in ~4–5 h without intervention
Allowed action bounds: combined = feed scale 0.8, air scale 1.15
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 dropped from ~10.5 to ~4.3 mg/L between 50 and 52 h while product (P=2.88 g/L at 48 h) tracks the source batches, indicating oxygen demand is outstripping transfer at peak growth. Without action DO2 will breach the 2.0 mg/L minimum within ~4–5 h, forfeiting product. A 15% air increase alone may not arrest the steep decline; a 20% feed reduction plus 15% aeration increase (combined) cuts OUR and raises OTR, giving the largest safe margin while retaining 80% of feed and most product mass.
args.uncertainty: The future oxygen-uptake trajectory is hidden; the 3 mg/L/h decline may stabilize on its own (as source dips did), in which case a feed cut sacrifices some product unnecessarily. Conversely, 15% extra air may be insufficient if OUR keeps growing. Delayed assays (4 h turnaround) and hidden states mean the 48 h P value may be stale by the decision time.
